evals.expected_output: In v9, Object3DNode (along with Node, BufferGeometryNode, MaterialNode, LightNode, MeshProps, etc.) was removed and the global JSX.IntrinsicElements augmentation pattern no longer applies (React 19 deprecated the global JSX namespace). Fix: augment the ThreeElements interface via module augmentation using ThreeElement<T>: declare module '@react-three/fiber' { interface ThreeElements { meshLineGeometry: ThreeElement<typeof MeshLineGeometry> } }. Alternatively use the v9 factory extend signature (const MeshLine = extend(MeshLineGeometry)) which infers types with no augmentation.
assertions: States that Object3DNode (and related *Node types) were removed in v9 and replaced by ThreeElement<T>
Replaces the global JSX.IntrinsicElements augmentation with `declare module '@react-three/fiber'` augmentation of the ThreeElements interface
Shows correct v9 syntax: ThreeElement<typeof MeshLineGeometry> inside interface ThreeElements
Optionally offers the factory extend form (const X = extend(Class)) as the augmentation-free alternative
Does NOT present the global JSX namespace pattern as still workable in v9

evals.prompt:
My custom point cloud renders nothing after upgrading React Three Fiber. The geometry code is:

```jsx
<points>
  <bufferGeometry>
    <bufferAttribute attach="attributes-position" count={positions.length / 3} array={positions} itemSize={3} />
  </bufferGeometry>
  <pointsMaterial size={0.05} />
</points>
```

It worked before the upgrade. What's wrong?
evals.expected_output: The count/array/itemSize prop form is the v8 pattern; in v9 a bufferAttribute must be constructed via constructor args: <bufferAttribute attach="attributes-position" args={[positions, 3]} />. Setting array/itemSize as props no longer initializes the attribute correctly.
assertions: Identifies the v8 count/array/itemSize prop form as the cause
Gives the v9 fix using constructor args: args={[positions, 3]}
Keeps attach="attributes-position"
Does NOT suggest the props form is fine and look elsewhere for the bug

evals.prompt:
I'm animating a mesh in React Three Fiber like this and my whole app gets janky:

```jsx
const [rotation, setRotation] = useState(0)
useFrame(() => setRotation((r) => r + 0.01))
return <mesh rotation-y={rotation}>...</mesh>
```

How should I do this instead?
evals.expected_output: Never setState inside useFrame — it re-renders the React tree every frame. Mutate the object through a ref instead: const ref = useRef(); useFrame((state, delta) => (ref.current.rotation.y += delta)); and use delta (seconds) rather than a fixed 0.01 so speed is refresh-rate independent.
assertions: States the rule that setState must never be called inside useFrame (per-frame re-renders cause the jank)
Rewrites the animation as a ref mutation inside useFrame
Uses the delta argument for frame-rate independent speed instead of a fixed increment
Does NOT propose throttling setState or memoizing as the primary fix

evals.prompt: In my React Three Fiber v9 app I want to construct the WebGLRenderer myself to tweak its constructor options. I remember doing gl={(canvas) => new THREE.WebGLRenderer({ canvas, logarithmicDepthBuffer: true })} — is that still right?
evals.expected_output: No — in v9 the Canvas gl callback receives the default constructor props (which include the canvas) instead of the bare canvas element: gl={(props) => new THREE.WebGLRenderer({ ...props, logarithmicDepthBuffer: true })}. The callback may also be async / return a Promise (which is how WebGPURenderer with await renderer.init() is supported).
assertions: States that in v9 the gl callback receives constructor props, not the canvas element
Shows spreading the received props into the renderer constructor
Mentions the callback can be async / return a Promise (WebGPU support)
Does NOT present the (canvas) => ... v8 signature as current

evals.prompt: I'm on React 18.3 and npm install @react-three/drei@latest fails with an ERESOLVE peer dependency error. Can I force-install it? What are my options?
evals.expected_output: Don't force it — drei v10 hard-requires @react-three/fiber ^9 and React ^19, and fiber v9 requires React >=19. On React 18 the compatible line is fiber v8 + drei v9, but that line is frozen (fiber's last v8 release was 8.18.0 in February 2025, no maintenance since). The real options: upgrade the app to React 19 and use fiber 9 + drei 10, or pin drei@9 + fiber@8 and accept no further updates.
assertions: States drei 10 requires fiber 9 and React 19 (peer deps), so force-installing on React 18 is broken, not a workaround
Identifies fiber 8 + drei 9 as the React 18 compatible pairing
Notes the v8 line is frozen/unmaintained (final release 8.18.0, Feb 2025)
Recommends upgrading to React 19 as the forward path

evals.prompt: To save battery I set <Canvas frameloop="demand"> in my R3F app. Now the scene only updates when I resize the window — my imperative camera tween and my custom pointer-driven mutations do nothing visible. What am I missing?
evals.expected_output: Under frameloop="demand" R3F only renders when it knows state changed. Imperative mutations outside React must request a frame with invalidate() (from useThree). Calls coalesce — invalidate() requests a frame rather than rendering immediately. Wire control/tween change events to invalidate (drei controls do this automatically when using frameloop="demand").
assertions: Explains that demand mode renders only on requested frames
Prescribes calling invalidate() (from useThree or the global export) after imperative mutations
Notes invalidate() coalesces/requests rather than renders synchronously
Mentions drei controls (or event wiring like controls.addEventListener('change', invalidate)) handle this automatically

evals.prompt: In React Three Fiber (three r185, meshStandardMaterial), my aoMap is baked against a separate UV layout, so I added a uv1 attribute to the geometry — but the material still ignores it and the AO looks wrong. What am I missing?
evals.expected_output: Since three r151 aoMap picks its UV set via aoMap.channel, which defaults to 0 (the base uv). Adding a uv1 attribute alone doesn't switch it — set material.aoMap.channel = 1 so it samples uv1 (the attribute that was named uv2 before r151). In R3F, set it on a ref, e.g. meshRef.current.material.aoMap.channel = 1 in a useEffect/useLayoutEffect. (With useGLTF, GLTFLoader already sets channel = 1 when the AO is authored on TEXCOORD_1.)
assertions: Identifies aoMap.channel (defaulting to 0 = the base uv) as why the uv1 attribute is ignored
Prescribes setting material.aoMap.channel = 1 so aoMap samples uv1
Notes that adding the uv1 attribute alone is insufficient without setting the channel
Names uv1 as the current attribute and uv2 only as the pre-r151 legacy name (does not prescribe uv2 as the fix)

evals.prompt: I added <EffectComposer><Bloom /></EffectComposer> from @react-three/postprocessing but I want only my neon sign mesh to glow, not the whole scene. How do I make just that one material bloom?
evals.expected_output: Raise the bloom luminanceThreshold above normal scene brightness and push the neon material's emissive past 1: <meshStandardMaterial emissive={color} emissiveIntensity={2+} toneMapped={false} /> — toneMapped={false} is required so the >1 values survive tone mapping and cross the threshold. (Alternatively mipmapBlur + Selection/Select from @react-three/postprocessing for true per-object selection.)
assertions: Pairs emissiveIntensity greater than 1 with toneMapped={false} on the glowing material
Uses luminanceThreshold on Bloom to exclude normal-brightness surfaces
Explains why toneMapped={false} matters (tone mapping clamps the >1 emissive values)
Optionally mentions Selection/Select as the explicit selective-bloom mechanism

evals.prompt: Using @react-three/rapier, I have a 2×1×4 (width × height × depth) box mesh and I'm adding an explicit collider: <CuboidCollider args={[2, 1, 4]} />. The box sinks halfway into other objects before colliding. Why?
evals.expected_output: CuboidCollider args are HALF-extents, not full sizes. For a 2×1×4 box the collider is args={[1, 0.5, 2]}. (Same convention family: BallCollider takes a radius; CapsuleCollider args are [halfHeight, radius].) The doubled collider explains the interpenetration offset.
assertions: States that Rapier cuboid collider args are half-extents
Gives the corrected args={[1, 0.5, 2]} for the 2×1×4 box
Connects the oversized collider to the observed sinking/offset behavior
Optionally notes CapsuleCollider's [halfHeight, radius] convention

evals.prompt: In @react-three/rapier, what's the difference between type="kinematicPosition" and type="kinematicVelocity" on a RigidBody, and which API calls move each one?
evals.expected_output: Both are script-driven bodies that push dynamic bodies but ignore forces. kinematicPosition is moved by setting target transforms each step: setNextKinematicTranslation / setNextKinematicRotation. kinematicVelocity is moved by setting velocities: setLinvel / setAngvel. (Fixed never moves; dynamic is force/impulse-driven via applyImpulse/addForce.)
assertions: kinematicPosition: moved via setNextKinematicTranslation/setNextKinematicRotation
kinematicVelocity: moved via setLinvel/setAngvel (velocity API), NOT setNextKinematic* calls
States kinematic bodies ignore forces/gravity but affect dynamic bodies
Does NOT swap the two control surfaces

evals.prompt: I'm using @react-three/postprocessing with <EffectComposer multisampling={8}><SMAA /></EffectComposer>. Edges still look shimmery and performance dropped. Anything wrong with this setup?
evals.expected_output: Don't stack MSAA with SMAA — when using SMAA (or FXAA) set multisampling={0} on the EffectComposer. Running both costs performance for no quality gain. Also keep AA as the last effect in the chain.
assertions: Says to set multisampling={0} when using SMAA/FXAA
Explains the redundancy/cost of stacking MSAA with post-process AA
Mentions anti-aliasing should come last in the effect ordering

evals.prompt: After migrating my R3F app from v8 to v9, the diffuse texture I feed into my custom ShaderMaterial looks washed out / too bright, but the same texture on a meshStandardMaterial looks correct. What changed?
evals.expected_output: v9 removed the automatic sRGB conversion R3F v8 applied to texture props. Built-in materials still get correct handling from three.js itself, but textures used in custom materials/shaders must be annotated manually: texture.colorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace (or texture-colorSpace={THREE.SRGBColorSpace} in JSX). Data textures (normal/roughness/etc.) stay linear — v8's blanket conversion used to corrupt those.
assertions: Attributes the change to v9 removing automatic sRGB conversion of texture props
Fix: set colorSpace = SRGBColorSpace on the color texture (property or pierced JSX prop)
Notes built-in materials are unaffected because three.js handles their color textures
Notes data textures must stay linear (and benefited from the change)

evals.prompt: An old tutorial says my aoMap won't show on a plain planeGeometry in React Three Fiber until I add a second UV set with geometry.setAttribute('uv2', geometry.attributes.uv). Is that still what I need on current three (r185)?
evals.expected_output: No — that's the pre-r151 recipe. Since three r151, aoMap defaults to channel 0, which reads the primary uv, and a planeGeometry already has a uv attribute — so aoMap already samples valid UVs on a plain plane. You don't need a second UV set, and copying uv into uv1 (uv2's current name) changes nothing while the channel stays 0. Only author a uv1 attribute and set material.aoMap.channel = 1 when the AO is baked against a separate UV layout. (If the map genuinely shows nothing, the cause is elsewhere — e.g. no ambient/environment light for AO to modulate, or aoMapIntensity at 0.)
assertions: Says the second-UV-set / uv2 recipe is stale (pre-r151) and not needed on a plain plane
Explains aoMap defaults to channel 0 = the primary uv, which a planeGeometry already has
Notes copying uv into uv1 is a no-op while the channel stays 0 (a distinct uv1 needs material.aoMap.channel = 1)
Names uv1 as the current attribute and uv2 only as the pre-r151 name (does not prescribe uv2 as the fix)
